Book a Meeting See our work Most SaaS companies have a great product and a broken go-to-market You've built something genuinely useful. Your sales team can close when they get in front of the right buyer. But your brand doesn't communicate your value clearly, your website isn't converting organic traffic into demos, and your demand generation activity is producing volume without quality. Customer Success as a Service for B2B SaaS | Booked Skip to content Booked Outsourced SDR Outsourced CS How It Works Blog FAQ Book a demo Outsourced SDR Outsourced CS For SaaS For B2B How It Works About Blog FAQ Contact Book a demo Home / Customer Success as a Service Customer Success as a Service Customer Success as a Service for growing B2B SaaS companies Booked builds and runs your Customer Success function: onboarding, adoption, customer health, early risk detection, value reviews and renewal readiness. You get a structured CS operation without the cost and time of building a large in house team. Book a Customer Success Health Check → See what's included Built for B2B SaaS Proactive, not a support desk Global, every time zone Monthly reporting on agreed KPIs What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function for B2B SaaS companies. Instead of hiring, training and managing a CS team, you bring in Booked to run the work that keeps customers: moving new accounts from purchase to first value, driving product adoption, monitoring customer health, stepping in early when an account is at risk, showing customers the value they are getting and preparing them for renewal. It works two ways. For companies with no CS team, or one where the founder still owns every customer relationship, Booked operates as the complete Customer Success function. For companies with a CS team that is stretched, Booked adds capacity and the operating infrastructure the team is missing: playbooks, health scoring, reporting and renewal workflows. What you buy is a capability, not hours: people, repeatable processes, lifecycle frameworks, health and risk systems, and reporting. This service is separate from Booked's outsourced SDR service and is run by its own team. Customer Success, not customer support Proactive outcomes, not reactive tickets Support fixes problems once a customer raises them. Customer Success works to stop those problems happening and makes sure customers reach the outcome they bought your product for. Customer support Customer Success Booked Mode Reactive, waits for a ticket Proactive, runs to a lifecycle plan Focus Resolving the issue in front of it Onboarding, adoption, value and renewal Measured on Response and resolution times Time to first value, adoption, health, at risk accounts actioned Sees risk When the customer complains Early, from usage, engagement and stakeholder signals Output Closed tickets Success plans, health scores, QBRs, renewal readiness The problem Your customer base is growing faster than your Customer Success function ✕ Founders and sales still own customers long after the business has outgrown that model. ✕ Onboarding is inconsistent , so time to value varies by who picked up the account. ✕ CSMs are buried in admin , onboarding coordination and repetitive work. ✕ No reliable health or risk process , so churn shows up at renewal instead of months before. ✕ Customer data is scattered across tools and nobody owns the full picture. Building it in house takes time you do not have A full internal CS function means hiring, management capacity and fixed cost before it delivers anything. In house Recruit, onboard, design the playbooks, then start In house Fixed headcount whether volume rises or dips With Booked Framework, people and reporting from one partner With Booked Capacity that scales with your customer count What we offer Four ways to work with Booked on Customer Success Start with a fixed scope build, hand over day to day Customer Success, or add capacity to the team you already have. CS Foundation A fixed scope project that builds your Customer Success framework: CS audit, customer journey, onboarding framework, segmentation, health model, playbooks, CRM and process design, and reporting. Fixed setup project Managed Customer Success Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts: onboarding, customer communications, adoption, health and risk monitoring, success plans, check ins, QBR support, renewal preparation, escalations, CRM and reporting. Monthly retainer CS Team Extension Additional CSM capacity working beside your existing team: onboarding, account management, adoption, health monitoring, QBR preparation, reporting and renewal preparation. Monthly retainer Customer Success Operations The systems behind Customer Success: CRM configuration, dashboards, health scoring, segmentation, lifecycle design, automation, SOPs, data cleanup and renewal workflows. Project or recurring retainer Our methodology The Customer Success lifecycle we run for every account Eight stages, from first conversation to expansion, so every customer gets the same standard of care. 1 Assess Goals, stakeholders, current state, risks and success criteria. 2 Onboard Implementation, training, milestones, responsibilities and first value. 3 Adopt Remove barriers so the product becomes part of normal workflows. 4 Monitor Health, engagement, usage, open issues and renewal context. 5 Intervene Act early when risk appears, with a clear owner and next action. 6 Demonstrate value Connect usage to the business outcomes the customer agreed. 7 Retain Renewal readiness and relationship health, well before the date. 8 Expand Spot genuine expansion needs and route them to your commercial team. What you get A working Customer Success operation, documented and yours Every engagement uses a standard set of tools and templates, calibrated to your product and customer segments. Customer success plans and account plans Onboarding and success milestone trackers Green, Amber, Red customer health scores and a risk register An owner, reason, next action and review date on every at risk account Escalation tracker with timeframes and documentation QBR and business review templates Renewal preparation checklist and expansion framework Monthly customer report against agreed KPIs Who it is for Built for growth stage B2B SaaS Typically 20 to 150 employees and 50 to 1,000+ business customers, sales led or hybrid, where Customer Success has become the bottleneck. No CS team yet 20 to 75 employees, 50 to 300 customers and a founder or small team carrying every relationship. We become your Customer Success function. A stretched CS team 50 to 150 employees, a few hundred to 1,000 customers and 3 to 10 CS staff. We add capacity, adoption support and CS infrastructure. Just raised or growing fast Funding, rapid customer acquisition, a major launch or international expansion that your current CS setup cannot absorb. Retention or renewal concerns No formal health model, weak onboarding or renewals that surprise you. We put structure and early warning in place. We usually work with Founders and CEOs, COOs, Heads of Customer Success and Operations leaders. How an engagement starts Diagnose first, then scope We do not pitch a package before we understand your customers. 1 Health Check A short Customer Success Health Check call to see where onboarding, adoption and retention are leaking. 2 Scope and success criteria A proposal tied to what we found, with two or three measurable KPIs agreed up front. 3 Kickoff and setup Stakeholder mapping, system access, segmentation, health setup and a 30 day implementation plan. 4 Run and report Customer facing work begins, with a monthly report and review against the agreed KPIs. How Booked compares with other ways to cover Customer Success Generic BPO or call centre: built for transactional, reactive support. Booked is outcome focused Customer Success, specialised in B2B SaaS. Freelance CSM: one person's capacity and no infrastructure. Booked brings a structured service with processes, tooling and reporting. Hiring internally: fixed cost and months of recruitment. Booked is flexible external capability you can scale up or down. CS consultancy: often stops at strategy. Booked builds the framework and then runs it. Global coverage, every time zone Booked supports B2B SaaS companies and their customers worldwide, across every time zone. Your contract sets the service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in, so check ins, QBRs and escalations happen during your customers' working day, not ours. Data protection and security Customer Success means handling your customers' data, so we treat data protection as part of the service, not an afterthought. Before any engagement starts we agree in writing how your customer data is handled, who can access it, and how it is returned or deleted when we finish. Access is limited to the people working on your account, protected by multi factor authentication, and removed at offboarding. If your procurement team needs a data processing agreement or a security questionnaire completed, we will work through it with you before kickoff. Questions Customer Success as a Service FAQ What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function. Booked builds and runs onboarding, adoption, customer health monitoring, risk management, value realisation and renewal readiness for B2B SaaS companies, either as the whole CS function or as extra capacity beside an existing team. How is Customer Success different from outsourced customer support? Customer support is reactive: it resolves tickets and issues when customers raise them. Customer Success is proactive: it moves customers through onboarding to first value, drives adoption, spots risk early and prepares accounts for renewal. Booked provides Customer Success, not a support desk or call centre. Who is it for? Growth stage B2B SaaS companies, typically 20 to 150 employees with roughly 50 to 1,000 or more business customers, where Customer Success has become a bottleneck but the business is not ready to build a large internal CS department. Common signs are founder led customer relationships, an overloaded CS team, inconsistent onboarding and no formal customer health model. What services are included? Four services: CS Foundation (a fixed scope build of your CS framework), Managed Customer Success (Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts), CS Team Extension (extra CSM capacity beside your team) and Customer Success Operations (CRM, health scoring, dashboards, automation and renewal workflows). How is it priced? Usually a one time setup fee plus a monthly retainer. The retainer is scoped by the number of managed accounts, their touch level, meeting cadence and reporting needs. CS Foundation and CS Operations projects are fixed scope. We do not bill by the hour except for tightly scoped projects. Do you guarantee retention or renewal rates? No. Retention and growth are outcomes the service is built to support, but product quality, pricing, customer budgets and market conditions also influence them. We agree two or three measurable success criteria at kickoff, such as onboarding completion, time to first value and at risk accounts actioned, and report against them every month. Which markets and time zones do you cover? We work with B2B SaaS companies globally and covers every time zone. Service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in are agreed up front and written into every contract, so your customers are looked after during their own working day, wherever they are. Is this the same team as your outsourced SDR service? No. Customer Success as a Service is run by a separate Booked division with its own team and methodology, and you can buy it on its own. Our outsourced SDR service fills the pipeline; Customer Success keeps and grows the customers you have already won. Find out where your customers are slipping Book a Customer Success Health Check. We will look at onboarding, adoption, health tracking and renewals, and tell you plainly where the gaps are and whether outsourcing is the right fix. Home Services B2B SaaS marketing Service B2B SaaS marketing measured in pipeline and MRR, not MQLs. An MQL is not revenue. A demo is not revenue. We get paid on the only B2B metric that is. By Mahesh Murthy , Founder of Pinstorm . Reviewed by Ansoo Gupta , Chief Operating Officer . Definition B2B SaaS performance marketing is the demand generation and go-to-market engine that turns a software product into qualified pipeline and recurring revenue — measured against the metrics a CFO actually cares about. Pinstorm runs it under an outcome-based agreement tied to pipeline created, CAC payback and net new MRR, so the agency's compensation moves with the revenue the SaaS business can actually book. B2B SaaS marketing has an accountability problem dressed up as a measurement solution. Agencies report MQLs, content downloads and webinar signups — numbers that feel like progress and correlate weakly with revenue. The pattern is always the same: demand-gen declares a record quarter on lead volume; sales closes a fraction of it; finance sees nothing in the bank. The two teams argue about lead quality, and the agency invoices regardless. The problem isn't that the metrics are wrong. It's that nobody in the chain is paid to make them right. An agency on a retainer is paid for activity, not outcomes. So they optimise for whatever fills a monthly report — which is never pipeline. We market SaaS the way a CFO would want it marketed: against qualified pipeline created, CAC payback period and net new MRR. Because Pinstorm's fee depends on those numbers, we have no incentive to inflate a lead count that finance will never see in the bank. If a channel generates traffic that never becomes opportunities, we cut it. That is not discipline — it is self-preservation. Who this engagement is for SaaS companies scaling past early product-led growth into a sales-led or hybrid motion. Companies that have product-market fit and a repeatable sale — but whose demand generation has plateaued, whose MQL-to-close rates are embarrassing, or whose CAC is climbing faster than the business can justify. Typically $1M to $20M ARR, Series A to C. The deal size is large enough that account-based approaches compound. The sales cycle is long enough that attribution requires thought. And the board is asking questions that MQL charts cannot answer. We are not the right fit for a pre-revenue SaaS company that needs positioning help and a logo. We are the right fit for a company that knows what it sells, who buys it, and why the current marketing motion is not converting into the revenue the model predicts. Demand generation tied to pipeline, not activity We build full-funnel demand: paid search and social to capture and create intent, content and SEO to own the categories buyers research before they ever fill in a form, ABM for the accounts large enough to justify the cost per touch, and lifecycle nurture that hands sales conversations rather than business cards. Every programme is instrumented to pipeline created and pipeline closed. Category-owning content earns search presence that paid cannot replicate and that continues producing pipeline after the article is published. Paid acquisition proves the funnel economics before SEO compounds. ABM concentrates resource on the accounts where deal size justifies it — and skips the ones where it doesn't. If a channel generates volume that never becomes opportunities, it is a cost to cut, not a KPI to celebrate. That is a sentence most agencies cannot say, because their retainer depends on running the channel regardless. CAC payback, NRR and the metrics that fund the company SaaS lives and dies on CAC payback and net revenue retention. The folk benchmark for payback is under 12 months for SMB motions, stretching to 18 for enterprise sales cycles — but your gross margin and churn rate set the real limit. A business that retains customers for five years at 80% gross margin can absorb a longer payback than one bleeding at the 12-month mark. We plan acquisition from your numbers, not from a benchmark chart someone published in 2019. Expansion and retention are part of the brief, not a hand-off. In subscription businesses, keeping and growing an existing account is cheaper than acquiring a new one. NRR above 110% compounds in ways that new logo acquisition alone cannot match — and every point of churn you stop is a point of marketing spend you don't have to replace. Pinstorm's compensation is structured against the KPIs agreed at the outset — an MRR milestone, a CAC payback ceiling, a pipeline volume target — and moves only when those numbers move. The terms are on paper before the first campaign runs. How we attribute pipeline in a long sales cycle B2B SaaS deals close in weeks or months, not days. Multi-touch attribution matters because the buyer who converts on a demo request in month four has been reading your content, seeing your ads and comparing you against competitors for months before that. Credit the demo form and you miss most of the actual influence. We work from your CRM data — Salesforce, HubSpot, or equivalent — and agree the attribution model and measurement window before we start. Typically: opportunity creation is the trigger that credits marketing, closed-won is the number that moves our fee. The window, the baseline and the minimum performance floor are written into the agreement. If your revenue cannot be tracked to marketing cleanly enough to compensate an agency on it, we say that before signing, not six months in. The ability to measure is a precondition of the model, not an aspiration. European B2B SaaS go-to-market Our Noordwijk practice focuses on European B2B SaaS go-to-market — typically for companies expanding from India or the Gulf into Western Europe, or for European-founded SaaS scaling across the continent. The operational model is the same: no retainer, outcome-based, tied to pipeline or MRR. European SaaS GTM has specific considerations: longer procurement cycles in enterprise accounts, GDPR constraints on data-driven prospecting, and genuine market fragmentation across languages and buying cultures. We navigate these from an office that has been operating in the market for years, not from a slide deck about pan-European expansion. What's included Demand generation across paid search, social and programmatic Account-based marketing (ABM) for target accounts Content and SEO for category ownership and search visibility Lifecycle and lead nurture tied to pipeline stages Pipeline, CAC-payback and MRR attribution Go-to-market strategy, positioning and messaging Expansion and net-revenue-retention programmes CRM attribution setup and measurement framework European go-to-market via Noordwijk practice The thinking behind it Advertising is a crappy business. So why did we start Pinstorm? No one gets rich in advertising - though it takes the same kind of smarts that any other unicorn does. So why bother? I'm Mahesh. I founded Pinstorm. Even after I swore to myself I … The world is changing. Is your marketing? A world where the industrial era practices of command-and-control or even Kotler-type 4P approaches simply don’t cut it any more. Proof in practice SaaS GTM That Actually Worked — 3× MRR in 8 months Taking a SaaS Business Global: 280% MRR Growth — 280% MRR growth Frequently asked What is B2B SaaS performance marketing? B2B SaaS performance marketing is demand generation and go-to-market activity tied directly to revenue outcomes — qualified pipeline created, CAC payback, and net new MRR — rather than to activity metrics like impressions or lead volume. It means the agency's fee is structured against the same numbers the board tracks, not against a media budget it manages. What does a B2B SaaS marketing agency do? It builds the full demand generation and go-to-market engine: paid media to capture and create intent, content and SEO to own the category questions buyers research, ABM for accounts worth winning, and lifecycle nurture that produces sales conversations. Pinstorm also owns the attribution layer — CRM-connected, pipeline-tied — because the agency's compensation depends on proving which activity drove revenue. Why does Pinstorm ignore MQLs? Because MQLs correlate weakly with revenue. Any agency can deliver MQL volume: gate a whitepaper, run a broad LinkedIn campaign, and watch the count climb while pipeline stays flat. We measure marketing on qualified pipeline created, CAC payback and net new MRR — the numbers that fund a SaaS business — and we are paid on those, not on a lead count sales will quietly ignore. What kind of SaaS company is Pinstorm the right fit for? Companies that have product-market fit and a repeatable sale, typically $1M to $20M ARR, scaling from product-led into sales-led or hybrid go-to-market. The model requires that revenue can be attributed to marketing activity — which means an operating CRM, a defined sales process, and a willingness to share the data. Pre-revenue or very early-stage startups are usually not the right fit; the model cannot price a business with no baseline. How does Pinstorm attribute pipeline in a long B2B sales cycle? We work from your CRM — Salesforce, HubSpot, or equivalent — and agree the attribution model and measurement window before the first campaign runs. Typically, opportunity creation is the trigger that credits marketing activity; closed-won revenue is the number that moves our fee. The baseline, the target, the attribution window and the minimum performance floor are written into the agreement. If revenue cannot be tracked cleanly enough to compensate an agency on it, we say so before signing. Does Pinstorm work with European SaaS companies? Yes. Our Noordwijk office focuses on European B2B SaaS go-to-market — for companies expanding from India or the Gulf into Western Europe, and for European-founded SaaS scaling across the continent. Same model: no retainer, paid on pipeline or MRR. European engagements account for longer procurement cycles, GDPR-constrained prospecting, and genuine market fragmentation. How much does B2B SaaS performance marketing cost? There is no retainer to quote. Engagements are structured against pipeline and MRR: an agreed baseline, a target, and a compensation that arrives when the numbers do. Media and tooling costs stay with the client. Our fee moves with the pipeline. The terms are on paper before the first campaign runs — so both sides know exactly what ‘working’ means before anyone spends anything. What is a good CAC payback period for SaaS? The folk benchmark is under 12 months for SMB motions, stretching to 18 for enterprise. But gross margin and churn rate set the real ceiling — a business that retains customers for five years at high gross margin can tolerate a longer payback than one losing them at 12 months. We plan acquisition from your actual numbers, not from a benchmark chart. How do we generate more B2B SaaS leads? Wrong target. More leads is easy and mostly worthless: gate a PDF and watch the MQL count climb while pipeline stays flat. The right question is: where are qualified buyers researching the problem your product solves, and are you visible there? Generate demand in those places, capture the intent that already exists, nurture toward sales conversations, and measure pipeline created — not forms filled. Does account-based marketing actually work for SaaS? For the right motion, yes. ABM pays when deals are large, the addressable market is finite and sales can act on the signal quickly. It is a waste of budget as a fashion statement bolted onto a high-velocity, small-deal motion. We use ABM where average contract value justifies the cost per account — and route the same budget elsewhere when it doesn't. Should a SaaS company invest in SEO or paid acquisition first? They compound differently. Paid acquisition buys pipeline this quarter; content and SEO own the category questions buyers ask for years. Early on, paid usually has to prove the funnel economics work before SEO is worth scaling. But every quarter you delay owning your category’s search terms, a competitor is claiming them. The split is a CAC payback calculation, not a philosophical stance. Pinstorm runs it under an outcome-based agreement tied to pipeline created, CAC payback and net new MRR, so the agency's compensation moves with the revenue the SaaS business can actually book. B2B SaaS marketing has an accountability problem dressed up as a measurement solution. Agencies report MQLs, content downloads and webinar signups — numbers that feel like progress and correlate weakly with revenue. The pattern is always the same: demand-gen declares a record quarter on lead volume; sales closes a fraction of it; finance sees nothing in the bank. The two teams argue about lead quality, and the agency invoices regardless. The problem isn't that the metrics are wrong. It's that nobody in the chain is paid to make them right. An agency on a retainer is paid for activity, not outcomes. So they optimise for whatever fills a monthly report — which is never pipeline. We market SaaS the way a CFO would want it marketed: against qualified pipeline created, CAC payback period and net new MRR. Because Pinstorm's fee depends on those numbers, we have no incentive to inflate a lead count that finance will never see in the bank. If a channel generates traffic that never becomes opportunities, we cut it. That is not discipline — it is self-preservation. Who this engagement is for SaaS companies scaling past early product-led growth into a sales-led or hybrid motion. Companies that have product-market fit and a repeatable sale — but whose demand generation has plateaued, whose MQL-to-close rates are embarrassing, or whose CAC is climbing faster than the business can justify. Typically $1M to $20M ARR, Series A to C. The deal size is large enough that account-based approaches compound. The sales cycle is long enough that attribution requires thought. And the board is asking questions that MQL charts cannot answer. We are not the right fit for a pre-revenue SaaS company that needs positioning help and a logo. We are the right fit for a company that knows what it sells, who buys it, and why the current marketing motion is not converting into the revenue the model predicts. Demand generation tied to pipeline, not activity We build full-funnel demand: paid search and social to capture and create intent, content and SEO to own the categories buyers research before they ever fill in a form, ABM for the accounts large enough to justify the cost per touch, and lifecycle nurture that hands sales conversations rather than business cards. Every programme is instrumented to pipeline created and pipeline closed. Category-owning content earns search presence that paid cannot replicate and that continues producing pipeline after the article is published. Paid acquisition proves the funnel economics before SEO compounds. ABM concentrates resource on the accounts where deal size justifies it — and skips the ones where it doesn't. If a channel generates volume that never becomes opportunities, it is a cost to cut, not a KPI to celebrate. That is a sentence most agencies cannot say, because their retainer depends on running the channel regardless. CAC payback, NRR and the metrics that fund the company SaaS lives and dies on CAC payback and net revenue retention. The folk benchmark for payback is under 12 months for SMB motions, stretching to 18 for enterprise sales cycles — but your gross margin and churn rate set the real limit. A business that retains customers for five years at 80% gross margin can absorb a longer payback than one bleeding at the 12-month mark. We plan acquisition from your numbers, not from a benchmark chart someone published in 2019. Expansion and retention are part of the brief, not a hand-off. In subscription businesses, keeping and growing an existing account is cheaper than acquiring a new one. NRR above 110% compounds in ways that new logo acquisition alone cannot match — and every point of churn you stop is a point of marketing spend you don't have to replace. Pinstorm's compensation is structured against the KPIs agreed at the outset — an MRR milestone, a CAC payback ceiling, a pipeline volume target — and moves only when those numbers move. The terms are on paper before the first campaign runs. How we attribute pipeline in a long sales cycle B2B SaaS deals close in weeks or months, not days. Multi-touch attribution matters because the buyer who converts on a demo request in month four has been reading your content, seeing your ads and comparing you against competitors for months before that. Credit the demo form and you miss most of the actual influence. We work from your CRM data — Salesforce, HubSpot, or equivalent — and agree the attribution model and measurement window before we start. Typically: opportunity creation is the trigger that credits marketing, closed-won is the number that moves our fee. The window, the baseline and the minimum performance floor are written into the agreement. If your revenue cannot be tracked to marketing cleanly enough to compensate an agency on it, we say that before signing, not six months in. The ability to measure is a precondition of the model, not an aspiration. European B2B SaaS go-to-market Our Noordwijk practice focuses on European B2B SaaS go-to-market — typically for companies expanding from India or the Gulf into Western Europe, or for European-founded SaaS scaling across the continent. The operational model is the same: no retainer, outcome-based, tied to pipeline or MRR. European SaaS GTM has specific considerations: longer procurement cycles in enterprise accounts, GDPR constraints on data-driven prospecting, and genuine market fragmentation across languages and buying cultures. We navigate these from an office that has been operating in the market for years, not from a slide deck about pan-European expansion. What's included Demand generation across paid search, social and programmatic Account-based marketing (ABM) for target accounts Content and SEO for category ownership and search visibility Lifecycle and lead nurture tied to pipeline stages Pipeline, CAC-payback and MRR attribution Go-to-market strategy, positioning and messaging Expansion and net-revenue-retention programmes CRM attribution setup and measurement framework European go-to-market via Noordwijk practice The thinking behind it Advertising is a crappy business. So why did we start Pinstorm? No one gets rich in advertising - though it takes the same kind of smarts that any other unicorn does. So why bother? I'm Mahesh. I founded Pinstorm. Even after I swore to myself I … The world is changing. Is your marketing? A world where the industrial era practices of command-and-control or even Kotler-type 4P approaches simply don’t cut it any more. Proof in practice SaaS GTM That Actually Worked — 3× MRR in 8 months Taking a SaaS Business Global: 280% MRR Growth — 280% MRR growth Frequently asked What is B2B SaaS performance marketing? B2B SaaS performance marketing is demand generation and go-to-market activity tied directly to revenue outcomes — qualified pipeline created, CAC payback, and net new MRR — rather than to activity metrics like impressions or lead volume. It means the agency's fee is structured against the same numbers the board tracks, not against a media budget it manages. What does a B2B SaaS marketing agency do? It builds the full demand generation and go-to-market engine: paid media to capture and create intent, content and SEO to own the category questions buyers research, ABM for accounts worth winning, and lifecycle nurture that produces sales conversations. Pinstorm also owns the attribution layer — CRM-connected, pipeline-tied — because the agency's compensation depends on proving which activity drove revenue. Why does Pinstorm ignore MQLs? Because MQLs correlate weakly with revenue. Any agency can deliver MQL volume: gate a whitepaper, run a broad LinkedIn campaign, and watch the count climb while pipeline stays flat. We measure marketing on qualified pipeline created, CAC payback and net new MRR — the numbers that fund a SaaS business — and we are paid on those, not on a lead count sales will quietly ignore. What kind of SaaS company is Pinstorm the right fit for? Companies that have product-market fit and a repeatable sale, typically $1M to $20M ARR, scaling from product-led into sales-led or hybrid go-to-market. The model requires that revenue can be attributed to marketing activity — which means an operating CRM, a defined sales process, and a willingness to share the data. Pre-revenue or very early-stage startups are usually not the right fit; the model cannot price a business with no baseline. How does Pinstorm attribute pipeline in a long B2B sales cycle? We work from your CRM — Salesforce, HubSpot, or equivalent — and agree the attribution model and measurement window before the first campaign runs. Typically, opportunity creation is the trigger that credits marketing activity; closed-won revenue is the number that moves our fee. The baseline, the target, the attribution window and the minimum performance floor are written into the agreement. If revenue cannot be tracked cleanly enough to compensate an agency on it, we say so before signing. Does Pinstorm work with European SaaS companies? Yes. Our Noordwijk office focuses on European B2B SaaS go-to-market — for companies expanding from India or the Gulf into Western Europe, and for European-founded SaaS scaling across the continent. Same model: no retainer, paid on pipeline or MRR. European engagements account for longer procurement cycles, GDPR-constrained prospecting, and genuine market fragmentation. How much does B2B SaaS performance marketing cost? There is no retainer to quote. Engagements are structured against pipeline and MRR: an agreed baseline, a target, and a compensation that arrives when the numbers do. Media and tooling costs stay with the client. Our fee moves with the pipeline. The terms are on paper before the first campaign runs — so both sides know exactly what ‘working’ means before anyone spends anything. What is a good CAC payback period for SaaS? The folk benchmark is under 12 months for SMB motions, stretching to 18 for enterprise. But gross margin and churn rate set the real ceiling — a business that retains customers for five years at high gross margin can tolerate a longer payback than one losing them at 12 months. We plan acquisition from your actual numbers, not from a benchmark chart. How do we generate more B2B SaaS leads? Wrong target. More leads is easy and mostly worthless: gate a PDF and watch the MQL count climb while pipeline stays flat. The right question is: where are qualified buyers researching the problem your product solves, and are you visible there? Generate demand in those places, capture the intent that already exists, nurture toward sales conversations, and measure pipeline created — not forms filled. Does account-based marketing actually work for SaaS? For the right motion, yes. ABM pays when deals are large, the addressable market is finite and sales can act on the signal quickly. It is a waste of budget as a fashion statement bolted onto a high-velocity, small-deal motion. We use ABM where average contract value justifies the cost per account — and route the same budget elsewhere when it doesn't. Should a SaaS company invest in SEO or paid acquisition first? They compound differently. Paid acquisition buys pipeline this quarter; content and SEO own the category questions buyers ask for years. Early on, paid usually has to prove the funnel economics work before SEO is worth scaling. But every quarter you delay owning your category’s search terms, a competitor is claiming them. The split is a CAC payback calculation, not a philosophical stance. Fractional Product Executive for B2B SaaS and AI Transformation | Erica Jenkins Skip to content How we help Sound familiar? Insights Resources About Start a conversation Scaling B2B SaaS is a marathon. Doing it while going AI-first is a gauntlet. I’m a fractional product executive for martech and big data SaaS, with 30,000+ hours, $500M+ in revenue, two acquisitions and an IPO behind me. With my bench of seasoned operators, we don’t just suggest change. We execute it, closing the gap between your vision and the tactical reality. Start a conversation See how we help Erica Jenkins, founder of Erica Jenkins Consulting The four root causes of stagnation Scaling from $10M to $30M ARR is hard enough. Trying to 5X that growth while moving to an AI-first architecture is harder, and “AI transformation” on its own won’t get you there. When growth stalls, it’s almost always one of these four. We fix them with your team, not around them. Innovation and tech debt AI isn’t a plug-in. It’s a foundational shift. We prioritize refactoring legacy infrastructure so tech debt doesn’t become AI bankruptcy, and modernize your stack so AI strengthens your product instead of bloating it. Leadership evolution The hands-on founder model breaks around $10M ARR. We help founders move from doer to architect, with fractional leaders running product, engineering and go-to-market while your internal team levels up. Operational communication Silos and egos block growth. We get product, sales and engineering working together on AI implementation, so internal automation turns into customer value instead of internal friction. Hardened processes We define and document the machine behind your SaaS, from AI-augmented customer onboarding to automated licensing, and build the repeatable playbooks that make you an attractive acquisition target. Three ways to work together We can work in your business, on your business or about your business. Each puts us at a different distance from your day-to-day, so choose the one that fits what you need now. Many clients move between them over time. Three rings around your team: In the business is closest, On the business is in the middle, About the business is outermost About On In Your team The closer the ring, the closer we work to your day-to-day. In the business Fractional Product Leader Two days a week, embedded with your team We lead product execution or a platform migration, set priorities, and build the habits that keep your company customer-centric and churn low. AI gets built into how your product team researches, plans and ships. On the business Product Optimization One day a week, across teams We assess how you build, launch and support your product, then put the roadmap process and playbooks in place so your teams work from the same plan, with AI and automation taking out manual work wherever it pays off. About the business Advisement Retainer Ten hours a month, cancel anytime Working sessions with your executives to unblock product, pricing and operating decisions, including where AI belongs in your strategy and where it doesn’t, with clear recommendations you can act on. Compare the engagements “ Fractional in title, full time on impact. Michelle A CEO & Founder What changes when we’re in the room Two recent engagements. Clients stay with us for two and a half years on average, so the work goes past recommendations into results. Media monitoring SaaS, $20M+ ARR From closed deal to customer login, automatically Before Every step from a signed deal to a working account was manual: someone had to set up the account, configure the package and send the welcome. Deal signed → Manual setup → Manual config → Manual welcome What we did With me as fractional head of product, we built a deal-to-provision flow that sets up each account automatically based on the package sold. Result Revenue leakage was eliminated due to automated provisioning, renewal and removing sales rep “giveaway” behaviors. We unlocked aggregated reporting of accounts. Deal signed → Automatic provisioning → Instant invite B2B SaaS company From feature factory to a story customers care about Before The roadmap was a feature factory, and every message explained how features worked, click by click. The company had also gone so far into product-led growth, down to buying on the website, that customers who needed help had no one to call. What we did We spent a quarter measuring the value customers actually got, then rebuilt the story around the problems the product solves. That reshaped the website and go-to-market, launched a customer newsletter and webinar series, and found a middle ground between self-serve and human help. Result −7% Churn dropped by 7%. From bootstrapped to two acquisitions and an IPO I co-founded and scaled a SaaS company to acquisition, then led product as a CPO through two more acquisitions. Today I bring that experience into growth-stage teams. Clients stay an average of two and a half years, and many still call when something big comes up. 30,000+ hours leading B2B SaaS product, customer success and go-to-market $500M+ in revenue under my watch 2× acquired, plus 1 IPO 2.5 yrs average client relationship What clients and colleagues say “I reached out to Erica at a critical time when our product strategy was key and execution required experienced leadership. Erica quickly integrated into our team and took ownership of the product by connecting with the team, our technology and our customers. She leaned hard into big challenges, modernized our product, increased customer engagement, and leveled up cross-functional work across the org. Fractional in title, full time on impact.” Michelle A CEO & Founder “I’ve had the opportunity to work with Erica early in my career as a colleague and more recently in her role as an industry-leading fractional product executive. In both cases, I witnessed firsthand her unique ability to translate a broad strategic vision into meaningful business results. Whether shaping product strategy, building roadmaps, accelerating go-to-market plans, or driving execution, Erica makes great things happen.” Daren B CCO “Erica was a valuable consulting resource during a major redesign and go-to-market launch. She is a perfect balance of strategy and execution and not afraid to roll up her sleeves to get things done. We’ve been collaborating since August of 2023 and she’s still my go-to for advice and advisement.” Tatiana F CEO & Founder, zLinq Things you’ll hear me say Straight talk I use with every client. Quite honestly, if one of these stings a little, it’s probably worth a conversation. That’s not a goal. That’s an outcome. When “get acquired” is the whole strategy. Sound familiar? Busy isn’t the same as building. When the roadmap is full, but customers aren’t using what ships. Sound familiar? Stop the demo tour. Start with the problem. When prospects sit through features and still don’t buy. Sound familiar? If product doesn’t know, product can’t fix it. When sales and customer success complain, and product never hears it. Sound familiar? 1 + 1 should equal 3. When a partnership or integration doesn’t add up to more for the customer. Sound familiar? Paint the picture before you build it. When teams can’t see the goal until it’s already built. Sound familiar? Let’s move from modernization to market leadership. A short conversation is usually enough to see what’s holding growth back, whether we can help, and which engagement fits. E-commerce An e-commerce platform built from scratch in California As director of technology at a US e-commerce startup, I built its platform from the ground up and led teams in Australia and India: checkout, discounts, refunds, US sales tax and APIs that scale. What it changed An e-commerce platform built from scratch, from the first line of code. Engineering teams led across Australia, the United States and India. The hard parts of commerce solved for real: discounts, refunds, US sales tax and nexus, and APIs that scale. The situation Before Cloudless Labs, I was director of technology at a US e-commerce startup for about five years, from around 2012, building its platform from nothing: the architecture, the business logic, the front end, the APIs, the event-driven back end, the infrastructure and its security. A startup moves fast, but commerce is unforgiving: every bug is someone's money, and every rule has an exception. What I built The platform itself, from scratch, and the teams that built it with me, in Australia and India, with regular trips to the States. Along the way, I went deep into the parts of e-commerce that look simple from the outside and aren't: Discounts and refunds. Stacked promotions, partial refunds, refunds of discounted orders: each has to reconcile to the cent, every time. US sales tax and nexus. Which states can tax you depends on where you have presence, how much you sell there and how many orders you ship, and every state has its own rules and rates. It's a maze, and getting it wrong is expensive. APIs that scale. Traffic that spikes on a campaign, and order flows that must never lose a payment, which is where I learned event-driven architecture the hard way. The front end was Angular, before React became the default. It was the job that turned me from an engineer into a technology leader, and it taught me that technology decisions have a date on them: frameworks change, patterns change, and a team should build for today's business problems, not every imaginable future one. This is also where I left the Microsoft stack for Node.js, open source and AWS, a move I explain in why I ended up on AWS . Why it matters to you If you sell online, the edge cases are the business. I've built them myself, from the database up, and know where they hide. This course provides a practical introduction to money laundering and terrorism financing risks, along with a clear explanation of obligations under the Anti‑Money Laundering and Counter‑Terrorism Financing Act 2006 . Significant legislative amendments made in 2024, which come into effect in 2026, are reflected throughout the training. Designed for reporting entities across banking and financial services, the course equips staff with the knowledge required to understand AML/CTF risks, conduct customer due diligence, and meet AUSTRAC reporting obligations. Learners receive a certificate of completion to support regulatory compliance and audit requirements. Course Highlights Online, self‑paced AML/CTF training Tailored for Australian financial services and ADIs Covers AML/CTF risks, KYC, monitoring, and reporting Aligned to Australian AML/CTF legislation and AUSTRAC guidance Introductory content for all staff with advanced modules for managers Audit‑ready reporting through Salt™ Compliance LMS Certificate of completion for compliance records Understanding Anti‑Money Laundering Risks Money laundering is the process by which funds obtained through criminal activity are given the appearance of having come from a legitimate source. These funds may be linked to drug trafficking, organised crime, terrorism financing, tax evasion, or other serious offences. In Australia, money laundering is often associated with organised crime and poses significant risks to the integrity of the financial system. Reporting entities must implement appropriate controls to detect, prevent, and report suspicious activity. Failure to manage money laundering and terrorism financing risks can result in regulatory action, criminal penalties, and serious reputational damage for organisations and individuals. Key AML Concepts Understanding anti‑money laundering is essential for protecting financial institutions and the broader economy. Core concepts covered in this course include: The stages of money laundering and terrorism financing Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Identifying beneficial owners, signatories, and agents Politically exposed persons (PEPs) and sanctions obligations Ongoing monitoring and suspicious transaction indicators Why Compliance Matters Non‑compliance with Australian AML/CTF obligations can lead to: AUSTRAC enforcement action Civil and criminal penalties Reputational and operational damage Increased exposure to financial crime Effective AML/CTF training ensures staff understand their responsibilities, can identify suspicious behaviour, and know how to respond appropriately. A strong training program supports governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance. This online Anti‑Money Laundering course helps Australian financial services organisations meet AML/CTF obligations by providing staff with a practical understanding of money laundering risks, customer due diligence, and AUSTRAC reporting. Course Outline Module 1: Introducing AML/CTF (all staff) Module 2: Money laundering and terrorism financing methodologies (all staff) Module 3: Customer due diligence (all staff) Module 4: Ongoing customer monitoring (all staff) Module 5: Reporting to AUSTRAC (all staff) Module 6: AML/CTF for managers (specialist roles) Who should do this training? Employees of reporting entities subject to Australian AML/CTF obligations. Does the course reflect the 2026 AML/CTF changes? Yes. The course reflects legislative amendments made in 2024 that come into effect in 2026. Does the course cover AUSTRAC reporting? Yes. Suspicious Matter Reports, Threshold Transaction Reports, and other reporting obligations are covered. Is this suitable for all staff levels? Yes. ### Our unique technological capabilities, multi-faceted investment strategies and culture of integrity shape our position as a leading financial services provider.

Northern Trust Corporation is a preeminent global financial institution that provides asset servicing, investment management and wealth management services for institutions, high net-worth individuals and families. For more than 135 years, Northern Trust has earned distinction as an industry leader for exceptional service, financial expertise, integrity and innovation. Today, we have more than 24,000+ employees around the globe and manage more than $2.0 trillion (as of September 30, 2026) in assets for our clients.

We earn our clients’ trust by staying true to our steadfast fiduciary heritage and providing exceptional service tailored to each client’s specific needs. Our market-leading technological capabilities allow us to deliver the highest level of service to our clients with speed and precision.

### Asset Servicing

Our Asset Servicing business is responding to the growing complexity of our clients’ needs with patented technology and customized financial solutions. Services provided include trust, custody, treasury, banking, and analytical/reporting solutions.

*   [![Image 2: View Alternative Asset Services](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-1126322217-wealthmangmt10_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/alternative-asset-services)  ### [Alternative Asset Services](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/alternative-asset-services)  
Ranging from regulatory and reporting compliance to complex alternative investment strategies, our solutions can help you stay aligned with the changing alternative investment landscape.  
*   [![Image 3: View Front and Middle Office Solutions](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-1187179171-frontmiddleoffice-1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/front-middle-office-solutions)  ### [Front and Middle Office Solutions](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/front-middle-office-solutions)  
Our tailored services can help you meet the changing demands for operational efficiency, data governance, risk management, cost control and business growth.  
*   [![Image 4: View Capital Markets](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-509031122_asset-servicing-capitalmarkets_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/capital-markets)  ### [Capital Markets](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing/capital-markets)  
Enhance the efficiency of your investment portfolio through our advanced technology, transparent trading, quality execution and optimized liquidity solutions.  

[GO TO ASSET SERVICING](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/asset-servicing)

### Investment Management

We are one of the world's largest asset managers, with approximately $1 trillion in assets under management. We construct innovative and efficient investment strategies that appropriately compensate investors for risk. Our services include mutual funds, ETFs, multi-asset solutions, retirement plan solutions and outsourced investment solutions.

*   [![Image 5: View Sustainable Investing](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-1173544006-invmangmt-sustainableinvesting1_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/investment-management/sustainable-investing)  ### [Sustainable Investing](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/investment-management/sustainable-investing)  
Our wide spectrum of sustainable approaches range from exclusionary to integration and thematic investing.  
*   [![Image 6: View Liquidity](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/hero/liquidity-iStock-182426549-1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/investment-management/liquidity)  ### [Liquidity](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/investment-management/liquidity)  
Our liquidity strategies—including operational, reserve and longer-term, strategic uses of cash—can be used to manage your liquid assets in accordance with your spectrum of investment needs.  

[GO TO INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/investment-management)

[GO TO U.S. INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT](https://ntam.northerntrust.com/)

### Wealth Management

As a market leader in wealth management services for high-net-worth individuals and families, we offer a full array of comprehensive solutions including financial planning, private banking, trust & estate services, philanthropy and family office services.Northern Trust has advised clients across generations and economic cycles, including the Great Depression, World War II and the 2008 financial crisis. With unmatched expertise and a culture built on client service, Northern Trust consistently ranks as one of the strongest global financial institutions in terms of financial strength and stability.  

*    [![Image 7: View Global Family Office Services](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-942365974-wealthmangmt-globalfamilyoffice1_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/wealth-management/global-family-office-services)  ### [Global Family Office Services](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/what-we-do/wealth-management/global-family-office-services)  
Our enterprise-wide global resources and cutting-edge technology power our comprehensive services for your family office, including advice-driven wealth management, investment management, banking and asset administration solutions.

*   [![Image 9: View Wealth Planning](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-1166773886-wealthmangmt12_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/insights-research/wealth-management/wealth-planning)  ### [Wealth Planning](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/insights-research/wealth-management/wealth-planning)  
Gain perspective and find ways to optimize your wealth plan through strategies covering taxes, wealth transfer, retirement plans and more.  
*   [![Image 10: View Market & Investment Trends](https://images.northerntrust.com/content/dam/northerntrust/pws/nt/images/what-we-do/iStock-1126202818-insightsresearch-marketinvsttrends1_1200x675.jpg)](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/insights-research/market-investment-trends)  ### [Market & Investment Trends](https://www.northerntrust.com/united-states/insights-research/market-investment-trends)

# Telehealth Enablement

**Great care, anywhere**

Healthcare Australia supplies credentialled clinicians and designs the virtual care models that help hospitals, aged care, community and government providers extend their reach and cover hard-to-staff hours and specialties, without compromising safety.

[Discuss Telehealth Solutions](https://healthcareaustralia.com.au/our-solutions/healthcare-education/telehealth-enablement/#modal-form-133)

Telehealth Is Now Core to Australian Care 

### 100 million+

MBS telehealth services delivered in the first two years (March 2020 to March 2022)

### 17 million

Australians who accessed telehealth over the same period

### 92,000+

Medical practitioners who have delivered telehealth

### 1 in 5

People had a telehealth consultation in 2024–25 (22.5%)

## More Than a Video Link

##### **Telehealth has moved from stopgap to standard. Delivering it well takes more than a video link.**

We help you design and staff telehealth services that extend your reach without compromising care. That covers sourcing experienced clinicians, building clinical workflows, training your staff in virtual care practice and supporting the technology, so patients receive safe, connected care wherever they are.

## Our Telehealth Solutions

*   Telehealth clinicians, after-hours and on-call coverage, triage and nurse-on-call
*   Access virtual consultation models and specialist telehealth
*   Remote patient monitoring
*   Hybrid care models that combine virtual and in-person care
*   Telehealth Nursing, psychology and EAP services

## Clinicians and Models That Make Telehealth Work

##### Technology is only half of telehealth. The other half is people.

We supply the qualified clinicians who deliver virtual care and help design the models around them, from triage and nurse-on-call to specialist consultations. Drawing on a national workforce, we can scale your service up or down and cover the hours, specialties and locations you can’t staff alone, without adding permanent headcount.

## Safe, Connected Virtual Care

**Behind every virtual consult is the technology and governance that keep telehealth secure, compliant and clinically sound.**

*   Consultation platforms: secure platforms, provided or integrated with yours

*   Clinician credentialling: registration, scope of practice and virtual care competency verified

*   Clinical governance: escalation pathways, documentation standards and incident management

*   Regulatory alignment: models designed around MBS requirements and National Board guidance on technology-based consultations

*   Privacy and data security: patient information handled in line with the Australian Privacy Principles

*   Service reporting: activity, response times and outcomes by site or program

**So virtual care meets the same standards patients expect from care in person.**

## Bring care closer, virtually

Whether you’re launching a new telehealth service or scaling an existing one, we’ll provide the clinicians, models and support to make virtual care work for your patients. Healthcare Australia is where care begins.

# Telehealth Enablement

**Great care, anywhere**

Healthcare Australia supplies credentialled clinicians and designs the virtual care models that help hospitals, aged care, community and government providers extend their reach and cover hard-to-staff hours and specialties, without compromising safety.

[Discuss Telehealth Solutions](https://healthcareaustralia.com.au/our-solutions/healthcare-education/telehealth-enablement/#modal-form-133)

Telehealth Is Now Core to Australian Care 

### 100 million+

MBS telehealth services delivered in the first two years (March 2020 to March 2022)

### 17 million

Australians who accessed telehealth over the same period

### 92,000+

Medical practitioners who have delivered telehealth

### 1 in 5

People had a telehealth consultation in 2024–25 (22.5%)

## More Than a Video Link

##### **Telehealth has moved from stopgap to standard. Delivering it well takes more than a video link.**

We help you design and staff telehealth services that extend your reach without compromising care. That covers sourcing experienced clinicians, building clinical workflows, training your staff in virtual care practice and supporting the technology, so patients receive safe, connected care wherever they are.

## Our Telehealth Solutions

*   Telehealth clinicians, after-hours and on-call coverage, triage and nurse-on-call
*   Access virtual consultation models and specialist telehealth
*   Remote patient monitoring
*   Hybrid care models that combine virtual and in-person care
*   Telehealth Nursing, psychology and EAP services

## Clinicians and Models That Make Telehealth Work

##### Technology is only half of telehealth. The other half is people.

We supply the qualified clinicians who deliver virtual care and help design the models around them, from triage and nurse-on-call to specialist consultations. Drawing on a national workforce, we can scale your service up or down and cover the hours, specialties and locations you can’t staff alone, without adding permanent headcount.

## Safe, Connected Virtual Care

**Behind every virtual consult is the technology and governance that keep telehealth secure, compliant and clinically sound.**

*   Consultation platforms: secure platforms, provided or integrated with yours

*   Clinician credentialling: registration, scope of practice and virtual care competency verified

*   Clinical governance: escalation pathways, documentation standards and incident management

*   Regulatory alignment: models designed around MBS requirements and National Board guidance on technology-based consultations

*   Privacy and data security: patient information handled in line with the Australian Privacy Principles

*   Service reporting: activity, response times and outcomes by site or program

**So virtual care meets the same standards patients expect from care in person.**

## Bring care closer, virtually

Whether you’re launching a new telehealth service or scaling an existing one, we’ll provide the clinicians, models and support to make virtual care work for your patients. Healthcare Australia is where care begins.

# About 24-7Healthcare

24-7Healthcare has over 30 years' experience in providing quality healthcare in the home, in community settings, at aged-care facilities, within a general practice and more recently through telemedicine.

Our Mission is “_**To provide exceptional healthcare when and where it is needed**”_.

We pride ourselves on clinical excellence and the delivery of exceptional service to patients. With services across nearly all of Australia, we are constantly expanding our network and service delivery areas.

24-7Healthcare works closely alongside a range of stakeholders in the provision of healthcare to ensure a collaborative approach to patient care.

*   Through 13SICK, we are the Provider of Choice in the after-hours with formal relationships to provide patient support services to more than half of all accredited General Practices operating in Australia.
*   Using our class-leading IT systems, we ensure a collaborative approach to health care, providing encrypted patient reports back to a patient’s regular GP to ensure continuity of care through appropriate clinical handover.  
*   Our telehealth services utilise state-of-the-art technology and provide you with access to a doctor anytime and anywhere.
*   Our network of Home Nurses, together with our network of GPs and after-hours Doctors, comprise the most extensive in-home network of healthcare practitioners in the country.
*   We have a national infrastructure and local teams to support you where you need us.
*   We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and you can always reach us 365 days a year.
*   Our Contact centre in Australia is a state of the art, secure facility.
*   Our mobile workforce utilises a purpose-built technology platform that operates in “real-time”, connecting our Nurses, Doctors and Patients.

### Our Values

![Image 7: Logo for 'we make a difference'](https://24-7healthcare.com.au/portals/0/Images/Our%20Vision/We%20make%20a%20difference-01.jpg?ver=2017-05-11-132628-693)**We make a difference:**  
 We play a vital role within the Australian health care system by providing healthcare services when and where they are needed most, whether it be our Nurses or our Doctors. We provide timely, efficient and high quality care to some of the most vulnerable members of our community.
![Image 8: Logo for 'we care for our patients'](https://24-7healthcare.com.au/portals/0/Images/Our%20Vision/We%20care-01.jpg?ver=2017-05-11-132628-660)**We care:**  
 It is our privilege to provide healthcare solutions to our patients in their homes, when they need us the most. We deeply care for our patients and our empathetic approach and the quality of care we provide are what truly sets us apart.
![Image 9: Logo for 'we lead the way'](https://24-7healthcare.com.au/portals/0/Images/Our%20Vision/We%20lead%20the%20way-01.jpg?ver=2017-05-11-132628-677)**We lead the way:**  
 We embrace ideas, innovative thinking and emerging technology to forge a better future for how Australians access and experience care at home. We merge our talents with technology to benefit the Patient and our People.
![Image 10: Logo for we are stronger together'](https://24-7healthcare.com.au/portals/0/Images/Our%20Vision/We%20are%20stronger%20together-01.jpg?ver=2017-05-11-132628-647)**We are stronger together:**  
 We celebrate the diversity of our talents and expertise to achieve as one great team. Our approach to industry and partnerships is collaborative, with a focus on leveraging strengths to drive better outcomes for our patients, doctors and nurses.
![Image 11: Logo for 'we are accountable'](https://24-7healthcare.com.au/portals/0/Images/Our%20Vision/We%20are%20accountable-01.jpg?ver=2017-05-11-132628-613)**We are accountable:**  
 We hold ourselves accountable to the highest ethical, clinical and professional standards. We continue to raise the bar of excellence and take very seriously the responsibility bestowed upon us to care for patients when they are in need.

About us | Centre for Healthcare Innovation Skip to main content Centre for Healthcare Innovation Menu Search Home Overview Testimonials PgCert PgDip MSt Fees, funding and support Applying FAQs About us More Home Overview Testimonials PgCert PgDip MSt Fees, funding and support Applying FAQs About us Search Menu Home Overview Testimonials PgCert PgDip MSt Fees, funding and support Applying FAQs About us Search Submit Home Staff Staff About us About Cambridge Cambridge is a world-leading centre for research and innovation in healthcare, underpinned by an extensive and vibrant community of clinicians, researchers, entrepreneurs, and commercial and public sector organisations. In response to a growing skills gap in the sector, the Healthcare Innovation programme has been developed by the Department of Engineering, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. Renowned for both its teaching and research, the Department of Engineering's aim is to address the world's most pressing challenges with science and technology. Since its foundation in 1875, the Department of Engineering has grown to become the largest department in the University and the largest integrated engineering department in the UK. The Department of Engineering’s bioengineering and healthcare research and teaching has expanded rapidly over the past few years, having been highlighted as a strategic research theme of the Department. The University of Cambridge performed strongly in REF 2021 (the UK's Research Excellence Framework assessment). The Department of Engineering submitted to the General Engineering Panel, in conjunction with Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology and Materials Science and Metallurgy, achieving a perfect score for our world-leading environment. The overall percentage of activity rated “world-leading” or “internationally excellent” was 99% – the highest score for any university submission to the General Engineering Panel. The Cambridge Biomedical Campus (CBC) is unmatched within the UK, and perhaps across the world, in terms of concentration of clinical, academic, educational, technology, pharmaceutical, and biosciences organisations.The CBC contains the University of Cambridge School of Clinical Medicine with its 12 Departments and associated Institutes, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, a major University Teaching Hospital with 1100 beds, Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust  and a number of directly funded research institutes. The programme benefits from its interactions with the vibrant local medtech/biotech industry in Cambridge. Companies in the Cambridge Cluster have an annual turnover currently at £51 billion and the area is home to 15,000 employees and 440+ companies in life sciences and healthcare. Professor of Healthcare Systems (TU Delft); Director of Cambridge Engineering Design Centre; Co-Director of Cambridge Public Health, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge; and Governor, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust Professor James Ward Course Director Research Professor, Associate Teaching Professor and Course Director, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, and Manager of the Centre for Engineering Better Care, Cambridge Biomedical Campus Unit Leads Dr Tom Bashford Unit 1 Lead: Research skills and innovation Assistant Professor in Healthcare Systems, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge and Consultant Neuroanaesthetist, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust Professor Michael Sutcliffe Unit 2 Lead: Healthcare Technologies I Professor of Biomedical Engineering and Head of the Mechanics, Materials and Design Division, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge Professor John Clarkson Unit 3 Lead: Healthcare Systems Improvement Professor of Engineering Design (University of Cambridge) and Professor of Healthcare Systems (TU Delft); Director of the Cambridge Engineering Design Centre and Co-Director of Cambridge Public Health, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge Dr Kirsten Rennie Unit 4 Lead: Patient and population health Clinical Epidemiologist and Senior Research Associate at MRC Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge Dr Saransh Sharma Unit 5 Lead: Healthcare technologies II University Assistant Professor in Bioelectronic Systems, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge Professor Jagjit Singh Srai Unit 6 Lead: Healthcare system innovation Director of Research, and Head, Centre for International Manufacturing, Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge Contact details For general enquiries on administrative matters, please email: HIP-admin@eng.cam.ac.uk For specific enquiries about course content, please email: healthcare-course-director@eng.cam.ac.uk Department of Engineering Trumpington Street Cambridge CB2 1PZ United Kingdom Tel: +44 (0)1223 332600 Most of the residential course teaching takes place in the main site Engineering Department at the Trumpington Street site, mailing address as above. The site is comprised of three buildings: the Baker building, the Inglis building, and the James Dyson Building. Visitors should report to the reception at the Baker building. ## The secure basis for your health data.

In the healthcare sector, it is essential to comply with industry-specific requirements, use scarce IT resources efficiently and process complex formats securely. Standard solutions from outside the industry quickly reach their limits here. Health insurance companies, pension insurance companies and service providers need tailor-made IT security.

With SITS Healthcare Services, you can protect sensitive data, meet compliance requirements and reduce the workload on your IT departments. This allows you to create a secure basis for digital communication with policyholders and partners.

*   **Full Compliance:**Fulfil requirements such as the Social Security Code (SGB), B3S-GKV/PV, B3S Medical Care, GDPR and NIS2 reliably.
*   **Less Effort:**Reduce support and IT costs with user-friendly processes.
*   **Future-proof:**Rely on solutions that are already established among leading health insurance companies.

*   **Industry-Specific Regulations:** Health insurers, pension funds, and service providers must reliably comply with requirements such as the Social Code (SGB), B3S-GKV/PV, B3S Medical Care, GDPR, and NIS2, as even small gaps can have legal consequences.
*   **Cost Pressure and Resource Shortages:** IT departments are under pressure to ensure security and compliance with tight budgets and limited skilled personnel.

## Frequently Asked Questions

 The most important answers about Cybersecurity in Healthcare 

Which regulatory requirements are covered?

Our solutions are compatible with requirements such as the Social Code (SGB), B3S-GKV/PV, B3S Medical Care, GDPR, and NIS2. This enables organisations to ensure audit and regulatory compliance.

How does PINaaS work?

PINaaS is a patented solution for digital PIN transmission. It covers the entire process – from initial registration and identification to use via app – and is secure, efficient and user-friendly.

For which organisations are the solutions suitable?

SITS Healthcare Services are aimed at statutory health insurance funds, pension insurance funds, social insurance institutions and their IT service providers and partners.

How can the solutions be integrated?

Products such as fideAS health and fideAS iam have a modular structure and can be seamlessly integrated into existing IT systems and processes without any breaks in workflow or complex system changes.

In the healthcare sector, it is essential to comply with industry-specific requirements, use scarce IT resources efficiently and process complex formats securely. Standard solutions from outside the industry quickly reach their limits here. Health insurance companies, pension insurance companies and service providers need tailor-made IT security.

With SITS Healthcare Services, you can protect sensitive data, meet compliance requirements and reduce the workload on your IT departments. This allows you to create a secure basis for digital communication with policyholders and partners.

*   **Full Compliance:**Fulfil requirements such as the Social Security Code (SGB), B3S-GKV/PV, B3S Medical Care, GDPR and NIS2 reliably.
*   **Less Effort:**Reduce support and IT costs with user-friendly processes.
*   **Future-proof:**Rely on solutions that are already established among leading health insurance companies.

For which organisations are the solutions suitable?

SITS Healthcare Services are aimed at statutory health insurance funds, pension insurance funds, social insurance institutions and their IT service providers and partners.

How can the solutions be integrated?

Products such as fideAS health and fideAS iam have a modular structure and can be seamlessly integrated into existing IT systems and processes without any breaks in workflow or complex system changes.
