## Professional Services Group (PSG)

The Professional Services Group provides timely, expert advice and assistance across the office on a diverse range of audit and related topics. PSG also provides direct support to the ANAO executive through independent quality reviews, the provision of advice and the preparation of responses to Australian Government reform.

[](https://www.anao.gov.au/careers/business-areas/professional-services-group-psg)

The Professional Services Group provides timely, expert advice and assistance across the ANAO on a diverse range of audit and related topics.

We provide direct support to the ANAO executive through independent quality reviews, the provision of advice and the preparation of responses to Australian Government reform. We also provide vital support to our financial statement, performance statements and performance auditors, including an up-to-date and comprehensive policy and guidance database; an audit methodology package including templates and guidance; and learning and development courses and information seminars. Most importantly, we offer well thought-out technical auditing and accounting advice to our auditors when they are in the field.

We contribute to the audit and accounting profession in Australia by providing client seminars that update ANAO clients on financial reporting developments and contractor briefings on topical public sector issues, as well as being an active member of the Australasian Council of Auditors-General (ACAG). We also support ANAO initiatives to build auditing capacity outside Australia by assisting the Indonesian Audit Office with quality assurance and audit support through the ANAO’s strategic partnership agreement with DFAT.

Our staff are afforded numerous opportunities to develop our technical knowledge through learning and development activities, as well as networking with policy agencies, professional bodies and other audit offices. A number of our staff also spend part of the year working on financial audits, thereby further developing their technical auditing and accounting skills.

Roles, requirements and responsibilities

### Job requirements

To be considered for a professional services position at the ANAO, you will require the following:

*   Accounting or other tertiary qualifications considered relevant by the delegate are highly desirable;
*   Strong accounting, financial or performance auditing/ analysis and/or IT technical skills;
*   Understanding of financial statements and related financial or performance audit risk-based methodologies and practices, including IT audit principles;
*   Demonstrated capacity to deliver less complex technical training and undertake technical research;
*   Good track record in project management; and
*   Australian Citizenship.

More senior positions also require:

*   Accounting and/or other relevant tertiary qualifications are highly desirable;
*   A professional background demonstrating superior accounting, financial management and/or auditing skills;
*   A strong track record in client and project management; and
*   Demonstrated capacity to lead and manage audit operations.

### Responsibilities

### Team member (APS Level 5)

Assist in the planning, co-ordination, development and conduct of performance or financial training for staff, undertake research and draft policy on less complex audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a sound level of professional and technical expertise and maintain internal and external client relationships.

Under the broad supervision and general guidance of the Team Leader/Director, positions at this level:

*   Assist in the planning, co-ordination, development and conduct of performance or financial training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on less complex audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a sound level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Maintain internal and external client relationships.

### Team leader (APS Level 6)

Plan, coordinate, develop and conduct performance or financial training for staff, undertaken research and provide policy on audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise and maintain internal and external client relationships.

Under the broad supervision and general guidance of the Senior Director/Director, positions at this level:

*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance or financial training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Maintain internal and external client relationships.

### Director (Executive Level 1)

Contribute to the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO, plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff, undertake research and provide policy on audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise, manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums and develop strategic solutions for the Branch and contribute to the achievement of corporate objectives.

Under the broad guidance of the Senior Director, positions at this level:

*   Contribute to the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO;
*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise;
*   Manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums; and
*   Develop strategic solutions for the Branch and contribute to the achievement of corporate objectives.

### Senior director (Executive Level 2)

Lead and manage a work area responsible for large, complex, high risk and strategically important audit services, manage the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO, plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff, develop strategic solutions for the Branch and make a significant contribution to the achievement of corporate objectives, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise and manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums.

Under the broad guidance of the Executive Director, positions at this level:

*   Lead and manage a work area responsible for large, complex, high risk and strategically important audit support services;
*   Manage the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO;
*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff;
*   Develop strategic solutions for the Branch and make a significant contribution to the achievement of corporate objectives;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums.

## Professional Services Group (PSG)

The Professional Services Group provides timely, expert advice and assistance across the office on a diverse range of audit and related topics. PSG also provides direct support to the ANAO executive through independent quality reviews, the provision of advice and the preparation of responses to Australian Government reform.

[](https://www.anao.gov.au/careers/business-areas/professional-services-group-psg)

The Professional Services Group provides timely, expert advice and assistance across the ANAO on a diverse range of audit and related topics.

We provide direct support to the ANAO executive through independent quality reviews, the provision of advice and the preparation of responses to Australian Government reform. We also provide vital support to our financial statement, performance statements and performance auditors, including an up-to-date and comprehensive policy and guidance database; an audit methodology package including templates and guidance; and learning and development courses and information seminars. Most importantly, we offer well thought-out technical auditing and accounting advice to our auditors when they are in the field.

We contribute to the audit and accounting profession in Australia by providing client seminars that update ANAO clients on financial reporting developments and contractor briefings on topical public sector issues, as well as being an active member of the Australasian Council of Auditors-General (ACAG). We also support ANAO initiatives to build auditing capacity outside Australia by assisting the Indonesian Audit Office with quality assurance and audit support through the ANAO’s strategic partnership agreement with DFAT.

Our staff are afforded numerous opportunities to develop our technical knowledge through learning and development activities, as well as networking with policy agencies, professional bodies and other audit offices. A number of our staff also spend part of the year working on financial audits, thereby further developing their technical auditing and accounting skills.

Roles, requirements and responsibilities

### Job requirements

To be considered for a professional services position at the ANAO, you will require the following:

*   Accounting or other tertiary qualifications considered relevant by the delegate are highly desirable;
*   Strong accounting, financial or performance auditing/ analysis and/or IT technical skills;
*   Understanding of financial statements and related financial or performance audit risk-based methodologies and practices, including IT audit principles;
*   Demonstrated capacity to deliver less complex technical training and undertake technical research;
*   Good track record in project management; and
*   Australian Citizenship.

More senior positions also require:

*   Accounting and/or other relevant tertiary qualifications are highly desirable;
*   A professional background demonstrating superior accounting, financial management and/or auditing skills;
*   A strong track record in client and project management; and
*   Demonstrated capacity to lead and manage audit operations.

### Responsibilities

### Team member (APS Level 5)

Assist in the planning, co-ordination, development and conduct of performance or financial training for staff, undertake research and draft policy on less complex audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a sound level of professional and technical expertise and maintain internal and external client relationships.

Under the broad supervision and general guidance of the Team Leader/Director, positions at this level:

*   Assist in the planning, co-ordination, development and conduct of performance or financial training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on less complex audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a sound level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Maintain internal and external client relationships.

### Team leader (APS Level 6)

Plan, coordinate, develop and conduct performance or financial training for staff, undertaken research and provide policy on audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise and maintain internal and external client relationships.

Under the broad supervision and general guidance of the Senior Director/Director, positions at this level:

*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance or financial training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Maintain internal and external client relationships.

### Director (Executive Level 1)

Contribute to the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO, plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff, undertake research and provide policy on audit matters, provide technical support, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise, manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums and develop strategic solutions for the Branch and contribute to the achievement of corporate objectives.

Under the broad guidance of the Senior Director, positions at this level:

*   Contribute to the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO;
*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff;
*   Undertake research and provide policy on audit matters;
*   Provide technical support for the business;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise;
*   Manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums; and
*   Develop strategic solutions for the Branch and contribute to the achievement of corporate objectives.

### Senior director (Executive Level 2)

Lead and manage a work area responsible for large, complex, high risk and strategically important audit services, manage the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO, plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff, develop strategic solutions for the Branch and make a significant contribution to the achievement of corporate objectives, exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise and manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums.

Under the broad guidance of the Executive Director, positions at this level:

*   Lead and manage a work area responsible for large, complex, high risk and strategically important audit support services;
*   Manage the development and implementation of audit methodologies and technologies in the ANAO;
*   Plan, co-ordinate, develop and conduct performance audit or financial audit training for staff;
*   Develop strategic solutions for the Branch and make a significant contribution to the achievement of corporate objectives;
*   Exercise quality control and a high level of professional and technical expertise; and
*   Manage client relationships including representing the ANAO in a variety of senior management and professional forums.

## Frequently Asked Questions

 The most important answers about our Professional Services 

What Are Professional Services?

Our Professional Services are specialized consulting and implementation offerings that help realize IT projects in a structured, secure and sustainable way. We support companies from planning through implementation and migration to optimization, rollouts and training. This ensures that new systems are not only introduced but also used successfully in the long term.

How do you ensure migrations run without downtime?

We follow a clear migration methodology: First, the existing environment is analyzed, followed by the creation of a detailed migration plan. Through pilot phases and testing, we ensure that systems are transferred seamlessly. Critical systems are always protected with fallback scenarios, so downtime is minimized.

Can rollouts also be carried out across multiple locations?

Yes. Our rollout teams are experienced in multi-site projects – both nationally and internationally. With standardized processes, centralized project management and coordinated logistics, we ensure that hardware or software rollouts are implemented efficiently and consistently.

Are the trainings tailored to each customer?

Yes. We adapt the content, format and language of our trainings to the specific target group – from end users to administrators. Whether in-person workshops, virtual trainings or on-demand videos, we ensure that employees receive exactly the knowledge they need for their daily work.

## Frequently Asked Questions

 The most important answers about our Professional Services 

What Are Professional Services?

Our Professional Services are specialized consulting and implementation offerings that help realize IT projects in a structured, secure and sustainable way. We support companies from planning through implementation and migration to optimization, rollouts and training. This ensures that new systems are not only introduced but also used successfully in the long term.

How do you ensure migrations run without downtime?

We follow a clear migration methodology: First, the existing environment is analyzed, followed by the creation of a detailed migration plan. Through pilot phases and testing, we ensure that systems are transferred seamlessly. Critical systems are always protected with fallback scenarios, so downtime is minimized.

Can rollouts also be carried out across multiple locations?

Yes. Our rollout teams are experienced in multi-site projects – both nationally and internationally. With standardized processes, centralized project management and coordinated logistics, we ensure that hardware or software rollouts are implemented efficiently and consistently.

Are the trainings tailored to each customer?

Yes. We adapt the content, format and language of our trainings to the specific target group – from end users to administrators. Whether in-person workshops, virtual trainings or on-demand videos, we ensure that employees receive exactly the knowledge they need for their daily work.

 Contact us now 

 We are happy to advise you!

Business & Technology Services is a provider of contract R&D and consultancy professional services with work experience in Australia (all States) and more than 10 countries. WBTS provides economic and technology services, including contract R&D activities for business, government, industry and private enterprises (small and large) in Less Developed, Developed and Developing Economies. In all our assignments we are searching for the extra yard, albeit through improved productivity, better market share, increased performance, sustainable growth, higher profits, better triple bottom line, improved governance or more satisfied clients. Projects have a focus towards corporate strategy; business planning; risk management; food security; competition policy; Internet strategy and web development; industry sector studies (with an emphasis on agriculture and agribusiness, food, pharmaceuticals, bioplastics, nutraceuticals and textiles); biotechnology; and institutional development including privatization, corporate governance and restructuring. We deal with both on-line and off-line situations and applications. Many of our projects have multi-functional dimensions and multi-functional teams to deal with technology, science, markets, structure and economics. The company name of Wondu is derived from the Australian aboriginal name for Eucalyptus wandoo – a long lasting, durable hardwood that thrives in the frequently difficult and changing environments of south-western Australia. It symbolizes our approach and philosophy that we believe we can make a difference to our clients, no matter what level of difficulty or complexity. That’s enabled us to work effectively in places like Central Asia, Eastern Europe, Africa, Latin America and East Asia Every task starts with a conscious purpose and a goal. This involves understanding and commitment by the most senior level of management and we start by seeking to identify the nature and extent of the problem or opportunity in question. We believe it is important to ask and define the right questions before identifying and assessing the options available. Solving problems typically involves a process of independent investigation and research. We add value by helping clients to organize and understand that knowledge, and if necessary, procure that knowledge. Often, the information and knowledge resides with the client’s workforce. This means recognizing the importance and value of people through all operating, supervisory and managerial levels or the organization. We aim to improve practical decision making throughout all areas of the organization to ensure a balanced and integrated approach to the process of implementation of changing technologies, organizational structures and work practices. With new discoveries and understanding of information comes more purpose and even new goals. That is the nature of our approach. There is no terminal point to knowledge, only new horizons to it. In this context, there is a “new economy” for every industry and firm, it is not confined to the information and communications sector. It extends very much into the so-called ‘traditional industries’. We are fully Australian owned although we work closely with local and offshore organizations. Wondu has completed assignments in Australia, Africa, East Asia, Central Asia, Latin America, Russia, United States and Western Europe. Wondu is a registered private company with the Australian Securities Commission [ACN 091 642 020]. Looking for an ABM partner that delivers pipeline and gets sales and marketing working together? Here’s what to look for, what to ask, and our approach Blog About Get in touch HubSpot Marketing Automation Your CRM should be working harder than your team is. Most HubSpot portals are set up once and left to gather dust. We build automation that actually reflects how modern SaaS buyers move so your team spends time on conversations, not admin. Book a strategy call See how it works Depth that only comes from doing this for a long time. We've been a HubSpot partner since 2014 which means we've seen every version of the platform, every shift in how B2B buyers behave, and every way a portal can quietly underperform. These aren't badges we chased. They're the result of genuinely specialising. HubSpot Partner since 2014 One of HubSpot's earliest agency partners globally, we've grown with the platform from day one. Partner Advisory Council, 2025 & 2026 Invited by HubSpot to help shape the platform's AI direction and roadmap, for two years running now. Software Industry Specialist HubSpot's specialist accreditation for the SaaS sector, built for how software companies actually work. The six places HubSpot quietly underperforms HubSpot is a powerful platform. But power without the right setup is just expensive noise. Here's where most portals and the teams running them quietly lose ground. Lifecycle Stages That Don't Match Reality Out-of-the-box lifecycle stages were designed for generic buyers. SaaS buying committees, trial users, expansion accounts and partner leads don't fit neatly into those boxes and most portals never get reconfigured to reflect that. No ARR or MRR in the Pipeline If your pipeline doesn't surface ARR, MRR, renewal dates and expansion potential, your sales team is flying blind on revenue quality. Most HubSpot setups track deal value, not the recurring revenue picture that actually matters in SaaS. No Renewal Pipeline Renewals are the most predictable revenue you have and most teams manage them through spreadsheets and calendar reminders. A properly built HubSpot portal has a dedicated renewal pipeline with automated alerts, health score triggers and handoff workflows. Sales and Marketing Running Different Data When marketing reports on MQLs and sales reports on pipeline, and neither number matches the other, trust breaks down fast. The real problem is usually a CRM that was never set up to create a single source of truth for both teams. Automation That Stops at the Lead Most HubSpot automation is built for lead capture and nurture, then it stops. The lifecycle continues through onboarding, expansion and renewal, and every handoff that happens without automation is a place where things fall through the cracks. Reporting That Can't Prove Marketing's Impact When the CFO asks what marketing contributed to revenue, the answer shouldn't be a shrug. Multi-touch attribution, influenced revenue and pipeline contribution reporting all live inside HubSpot but only if someone builds them properly. Success Story A brand new SaaS product launch and HubSpot automation that already knew who was ready to buy. OAHI launched into workforce management, one of the most crowded corners of SaaS, as a brand nobody had heard of yet. Great product, great team, no name recognition to lean on. Their HubSpot needed to work as hard as they did. So it does. Every visitor's journey is tracked automatically — which pages, in what order, how long they lingered — so OAHI's team can see who's still deciding and who's ready to talk, without guessing. Months in, OAHI had leads landing from across Australia and Asia-Pacific, a brand still finding its feet, with a pipeline solid enough that leadership noticed, and a team that never had to grow just to keep up. What We Build HubSpot configured for the way SaaS works. Not a generic setup. A portal built around your revenue model of ARR, MRR, renewals, expansion and the AI-era buyer journey. 01 ARR, MRR & Churn Pipeline ARR, MRR, expansion and churn risk tracked live in your pipeline, no more spreadsheets and no more guesswork. 02 Renewal Pipeline & Automation Health-score triggers, automated alerts and handoff workflows in a dedicated pipeline, so no renewal slips through. 03 Lifecycle Stage Architecture Custom stages that mirror how buyers move: trials, buying committees, expansion accounts and partner leads, mapped correctly. 04 AI-Era Lead Capture & Scoring Scoring built for informed buyers, weighing intent signals, content engagement and AI-referred traffic, not just form fills. 05 A Full Lifecycle Automation Automation from first touch through onboarding, handoff, expansion and renewal, covering every moment admin used to eat up. 06 Revenue Attribution Reporting Multi-touch attribution and pipeline contribution, so when the CFO asks what marketing did, you've got a real answer. Our HubSpot Process Go from audit to automation in only six steps. We don't start by rebuilding. We start by understanding what's already there and what it's actually costing you. Step 01 Portal Audit We go inside your existing portal and find where it's underperforming: data quality, lifecycle gaps, broken automation and reports nobody trusts. Step 02 Revenue Model Mapping We map your SaaS revenue model, ARR, MRR, expansion, renewals and churn risk, into a CRM architecture that reflects how you actually grow. Step 03 Lifecycle & Pipeline Build Custom lifecycle stages, pipeline views and deal properties configured for your buyer journey, not HubSpot's out-of-the-box defaults. Step 04 Automation Architecture We build the workflows your team needs across the full lifecycle: capture, nurture, sales handoff, onboarding, renewal and expansion triggers. Step 05 Reporting & Attribution Dashboards that give marketing, sales and leadership one version of the truth, including attribution reporting that proves pipeline impact. Step 06 Team Training & Handover We train your team on everything we've built, and why. A portal your team understands is a portal your team will actually use. Not sure if your HubSpot portal is set up for the way you actually work? That's exactly the kind of conversation Jo loves. No pitch, no pressure — just an honest look at what's working, what isn't, and whether there's a smarter way to set it up. Customer Success as a Service for B2B SaaS | Booked Skip to content Booked Outsourced SDR Outsourced CS How It Works Blog FAQ Book a demo Outsourced SDR Outsourced CS For SaaS For B2B How It Works About Blog FAQ Contact Book a demo Home / Customer Success as a Service Customer Success as a Service Customer Success as a Service for growing B2B SaaS companies Booked builds and runs your Customer Success function: onboarding, adoption, customer health, early risk detection, value reviews and renewal readiness. You get a structured CS operation without the cost and time of building a large in house team. Book a Customer Success Health Check → See what's included Built for B2B SaaS Proactive, not a support desk Global, every time zone Monthly reporting on agreed KPIs What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function for B2B SaaS companies. Instead of hiring, training and managing a CS team, you bring in Booked to run the work that keeps customers: moving new accounts from purchase to first value, driving product adoption, monitoring customer health, stepping in early when an account is at risk, showing customers the value they are getting and preparing them for renewal. It works two ways. For companies with no CS team, or one where the founder still owns every customer relationship, Booked operates as the complete Customer Success function. For companies with a CS team that is stretched, Booked adds capacity and the operating infrastructure the team is missing: playbooks, health scoring, reporting and renewal workflows. What you buy is a capability, not hours: people, repeatable processes, lifecycle frameworks, health and risk systems, and reporting. This service is separate from Booked's outsourced SDR service and is run by its own team. Customer Success, not customer support Proactive outcomes, not reactive tickets Support fixes problems once a customer raises them. Customer Success works to stop those problems happening and makes sure customers reach the outcome they bought your product for. Customer support Customer Success Booked Mode Reactive, waits for a ticket Proactive, runs to a lifecycle plan Focus Resolving the issue in front of it Onboarding, adoption, value and renewal Measured on Response and resolution times Time to first value, adoption, health, at risk accounts actioned Sees risk When the customer complains Early, from usage, engagement and stakeholder signals Output Closed tickets Success plans, health scores, QBRs, renewal readiness The problem Your customer base is growing faster than your Customer Success function ✕ Founders and sales still own customers long after the business has outgrown that model. ✕ Onboarding is inconsistent , so time to value varies by who picked up the account. ✕ CSMs are buried in admin , onboarding coordination and repetitive work. ✕ No reliable health or risk process , so churn shows up at renewal instead of months before. ✕ Customer data is scattered across tools and nobody owns the full picture. Building it in house takes time you do not have A full internal CS function means hiring, management capacity and fixed cost before it delivers anything. In house Recruit, onboard, design the playbooks, then start In house Fixed headcount whether volume rises or dips With Booked Framework, people and reporting from one partner With Booked Capacity that scales with your customer count What we offer Four ways to work with Booked on Customer Success Start with a fixed scope build, hand over day to day Customer Success, or add capacity to the team you already have. CS Foundation A fixed scope project that builds your Customer Success framework: CS audit, customer journey, onboarding framework, segmentation, health model, playbooks, CRM and process design, and reporting. Fixed setup project Managed Customer Success Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts: onboarding, customer communications, adoption, health and risk monitoring, success plans, check ins, QBR support, renewal preparation, escalations, CRM and reporting. Monthly retainer CS Team Extension Additional CSM capacity working beside your existing team: onboarding, account management, adoption, health monitoring, QBR preparation, reporting and renewal preparation. Monthly retainer Customer Success Operations The systems behind Customer Success: CRM configuration, dashboards, health scoring, segmentation, lifecycle design, automation, SOPs, data cleanup and renewal workflows. Project or recurring retainer Our methodology The Customer Success lifecycle we run for every account Eight stages, from first conversation to expansion, so every customer gets the same standard of care. 1 Assess Goals, stakeholders, current state, risks and success criteria. 2 Onboard Implementation, training, milestones, responsibilities and first value. 3 Adopt Remove barriers so the product becomes part of normal workflows. 4 Monitor Health, engagement, usage, open issues and renewal context. 5 Intervene Act early when risk appears, with a clear owner and next action. 6 Demonstrate value Connect usage to the business outcomes the customer agreed. 7 Retain Renewal readiness and relationship health, well before the date. 8 Expand Spot genuine expansion needs and route them to your commercial team. What you get A working Customer Success operation, documented and yours Every engagement uses a standard set of tools and templates, calibrated to your product and customer segments. Customer success plans and account plans Onboarding and success milestone trackers Green, Amber, Red customer health scores and a risk register An owner, reason, next action and review date on every at risk account Escalation tracker with timeframes and documentation QBR and business review templates Renewal preparation checklist and expansion framework Monthly customer report against agreed KPIs Who it is for Built for growth stage B2B SaaS Typically 20 to 150 employees and 50 to 1,000+ business customers, sales led or hybrid, where Customer Success has become the bottleneck. No CS team yet 20 to 75 employees, 50 to 300 customers and a founder or small team carrying every relationship. We become your Customer Success function. A stretched CS team 50 to 150 employees, a few hundred to 1,000 customers and 3 to 10 CS staff. We add capacity, adoption support and CS infrastructure. Just raised or growing fast Funding, rapid customer acquisition, a major launch or international expansion that your current CS setup cannot absorb. Retention or renewal concerns No formal health model, weak onboarding or renewals that surprise you. We put structure and early warning in place. We usually work with Founders and CEOs, COOs, Heads of Customer Success and Operations leaders. How an engagement starts Diagnose first, then scope We do not pitch a package before we understand your customers. 1 Health Check A short Customer Success Health Check call to see where onboarding, adoption and retention are leaking. 2 Scope and success criteria A proposal tied to what we found, with two or three measurable KPIs agreed up front. 3 Kickoff and setup Stakeholder mapping, system access, segmentation, health setup and a 30 day implementation plan. 4 Run and report Customer facing work begins, with a monthly report and review against the agreed KPIs. How Booked compares with other ways to cover Customer Success Generic BPO or call centre: built for transactional, reactive support. Booked is outcome focused Customer Success, specialised in B2B SaaS. Freelance CSM: one person's capacity and no infrastructure. Booked brings a structured service with processes, tooling and reporting. Hiring internally: fixed cost and months of recruitment. Booked is flexible external capability you can scale up or down. CS consultancy: often stops at strategy. Booked builds the framework and then runs it. Global coverage, every time zone Booked supports B2B SaaS companies and their customers worldwide, across every time zone. Your contract sets the service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in, so check ins, QBRs and escalations happen during your customers' working day, not ours. Data protection and security Customer Success means handling your customers' data, so we treat data protection as part of the service, not an afterthought. Before any engagement starts we agree in writing how your customer data is handled, who can access it, and how it is returned or deleted when we finish. Access is limited to the people working on your account, protected by multi factor authentication, and removed at offboarding. If your procurement team needs a data processing agreement or a security questionnaire completed, we will work through it with you before kickoff. Questions Customer Success as a Service FAQ What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function. Booked builds and runs onboarding, adoption, customer health monitoring, risk management, value realisation and renewal readiness for B2B SaaS companies, either as the whole CS function or as extra capacity beside an existing team. How is Customer Success different from outsourced customer support? Customer support is reactive: it resolves tickets and issues when customers raise them. Customer Success is proactive: it moves customers through onboarding to first value, drives adoption, spots risk early and prepares accounts for renewal. Booked provides Customer Success, not a support desk or call centre. Who is it for? Growth stage B2B SaaS companies, typically 20 to 150 employees with roughly 50 to 1,000 or more business customers, where Customer Success has become a bottleneck but the business is not ready to build a large internal CS department. Common signs are founder led customer relationships, an overloaded CS team, inconsistent onboarding and no formal customer health model. What services are included? Four services: CS Foundation (a fixed scope build of your CS framework), Managed Customer Success (Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts), CS Team Extension (extra CSM capacity beside your team) and Customer Success Operations (CRM, health scoring, dashboards, automation and renewal workflows). How is it priced? Usually a one time setup fee plus a monthly retainer. The retainer is scoped by the number of managed accounts, their touch level, meeting cadence and reporting needs. CS Foundation and CS Operations projects are fixed scope. We do not bill by the hour except for tightly scoped projects. Do you guarantee retention or renewal rates? No. Retention and growth are outcomes the service is built to support, but product quality, pricing, customer budgets and market conditions also influence them. We agree two or three measurable success criteria at kickoff, such as onboarding completion, time to first value and at risk accounts actioned, and report against them every month. Which markets and time zones do you cover? We work with B2B SaaS companies globally and covers every time zone. Service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in are agreed up front and written into every contract, so your customers are looked after during their own working day, wherever they are. Is this the same team as your outsourced SDR service? No. Customer Success as a Service is run by a separate Booked division with its own team and methodology, and you can buy it on its own. Our outsourced SDR service fills the pipeline; Customer Success keeps and grows the customers you have already won. Find out where your customers are slipping Book a Customer Success Health Check. We will look at onboarding, adoption, health tracking and renewals, and tell you plainly where the gaps are and whether outsourcing is the right fix. You get a structured CS operation without the cost and time of building a large in house team. Book a Customer Success Health Check → See what's included Built for B2B SaaS Proactive, not a support desk Global, every time zone Monthly reporting on agreed KPIs What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function for B2B SaaS companies. Instead of hiring, training and managing a CS team, you bring in Booked to run the work that keeps customers: moving new accounts from purchase to first value, driving product adoption, monitoring customer health, stepping in early when an account is at risk, showing customers the value they are getting and preparing them for renewal. It works two ways. For companies with no CS team, or one where the founder still owns every customer relationship, Booked operates as the complete Customer Success function. For companies with a CS team that is stretched, Booked adds capacity and the operating infrastructure the team is missing: playbooks, health scoring, reporting and renewal workflows. What you buy is a capability, not hours: people, repeatable processes, lifecycle frameworks, health and risk systems, and reporting. This service is separate from Booked's outsourced SDR service and is run by its own team. Customer Success, not customer support Proactive outcomes, not reactive tickets Support fixes problems once a customer raises them. Customer Success works to stop those problems happening and makes sure customers reach the outcome they bought your product for. Customer support Customer Success Booked Mode Reactive, waits for a ticket Proactive, runs to a lifecycle plan Focus Resolving the issue in front of it Onboarding, adoption, value and renewal Measured on Response and resolution times Time to first value, adoption, health, at risk accounts actioned Sees risk When the customer complains Early, from usage, engagement and stakeholder signals Output Closed tickets Success plans, health scores, QBRs, renewal readiness The problem Your customer base is growing faster than your Customer Success function ✕ Founders and sales still own customers long after the business has outgrown that model. ✕ Onboarding is inconsistent , so time to value varies by who picked up the account. ✕ CSMs are buried in admin , onboarding coordination and repetitive work. ✕ No reliable health or risk process , so churn shows up at renewal instead of months before. ✕ Customer data is scattered across tools and nobody owns the full picture. Building it in house takes time you do not have A full internal CS function means hiring, management capacity and fixed cost before it delivers anything. In house Recruit, onboard, design the playbooks, then start In house Fixed headcount whether volume rises or dips With Booked Framework, people and reporting from one partner With Booked Capacity that scales with your customer count What we offer Four ways to work with Booked on Customer Success Start with a fixed scope build, hand over day to day Customer Success, or add capacity to the team you already have. CS Foundation A fixed scope project that builds your Customer Success framework: CS audit, customer journey, onboarding framework, segmentation, health model, playbooks, CRM and process design, and reporting. Fixed setup project Managed Customer Success Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts: onboarding, customer communications, adoption, health and risk monitoring, success plans, check ins, QBR support, renewal preparation, escalations, CRM and reporting. Monthly retainer CS Team Extension Additional CSM capacity working beside your existing team: onboarding, account management, adoption, health monitoring, QBR preparation, reporting and renewal preparation. Monthly retainer Customer Success Operations The systems behind Customer Success: CRM configuration, dashboards, health scoring, segmentation, lifecycle design, automation, SOPs, data cleanup and renewal workflows. Project or recurring retainer Our methodology The Customer Success lifecycle we run for every account Eight stages, from first conversation to expansion, so every customer gets the same standard of care. 1 Assess Goals, stakeholders, current state, risks and success criteria. 2 Onboard Implementation, training, milestones, responsibilities and first value. 3 Adopt Remove barriers so the product becomes part of normal workflows. 4 Monitor Health, engagement, usage, open issues and renewal context. 5 Intervene Act early when risk appears, with a clear owner and next action. 6 Demonstrate value Connect usage to the business outcomes the customer agreed. 7 Retain Renewal readiness and relationship health, well before the date. 8 Expand Spot genuine expansion needs and route them to your commercial team. What you get A working Customer Success operation, documented and yours Every engagement uses a standard set of tools and templates, calibrated to your product and customer segments. Customer success plans and account plans Onboarding and success milestone trackers Green, Amber, Red customer health scores and a risk register An owner, reason, next action and review date on every at risk account Escalation tracker with timeframes and documentation QBR and business review templates Renewal preparation checklist and expansion framework Monthly customer report against agreed KPIs Who it is for Built for growth stage B2B SaaS Typically 20 to 150 employees and 50 to 1,000+ business customers, sales led or hybrid, where Customer Success has become the bottleneck. No CS team yet 20 to 75 employees, 50 to 300 customers and a founder or small team carrying every relationship. We become your Customer Success function. A stretched CS team 50 to 150 employees, a few hundred to 1,000 customers and 3 to 10 CS staff. We add capacity, adoption support and CS infrastructure. Just raised or growing fast Funding, rapid customer acquisition, a major launch or international expansion that your current CS setup cannot absorb. Retention or renewal concerns No formal health model, weak onboarding or renewals that surprise you. We put structure and early warning in place. We usually work with Founders and CEOs, COOs, Heads of Customer Success and Operations leaders. How an engagement starts Diagnose first, then scope We do not pitch a package before we understand your customers. 1 Health Check A short Customer Success Health Check call to see where onboarding, adoption and retention are leaking. 2 Scope and success criteria A proposal tied to what we found, with two or three measurable KPIs agreed up front. 3 Kickoff and setup Stakeholder mapping, system access, segmentation, health setup and a 30 day implementation plan. 4 Run and report Customer facing work begins, with a monthly report and review against the agreed KPIs. How Booked compares with other ways to cover Customer Success Generic BPO or call centre: built for transactional, reactive support. Booked is outcome focused Customer Success, specialised in B2B SaaS. Freelance CSM: one person's capacity and no infrastructure. Booked brings a structured service with processes, tooling and reporting. Hiring internally: fixed cost and months of recruitment. Booked is flexible external capability you can scale up or down. CS consultancy: often stops at strategy. Booked builds the framework and then runs it. Global coverage, every time zone Booked supports B2B SaaS companies and their customers worldwide, across every time zone. Your contract sets the service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in, so check ins, QBRs and escalations happen during your customers' working day, not ours. Data protection and security Customer Success means handling your customers' data, so we treat data protection as part of the service, not an afterthought. Before any engagement starts we agree in writing how your customer data is handled, who can access it, and how it is returned or deleted when we finish. Access is limited to the people working on your account, protected by multi factor authentication, and removed at offboarding. If your procurement team needs a data processing agreement or a security questionnaire completed, we will work through it with you before kickoff. Questions Customer Success as a Service FAQ What is Customer Success as a Service? Customer Success as a Service (CSaaS) is an outsourced Customer Success function. Booked builds and runs onboarding, adoption, customer health monitoring, risk management, value realisation and renewal readiness for B2B SaaS companies, either as the whole CS function or as extra capacity beside an existing team. How is Customer Success different from outsourced customer support? Customer support is reactive: it resolves tickets and issues when customers raise them. Customer Success is proactive: it moves customers through onboarding to first value, drives adoption, spots risk early and prepares accounts for renewal. Booked provides Customer Success, not a support desk or call centre. Who is it for? Growth stage B2B SaaS companies, typically 20 to 150 employees with roughly 50 to 1,000 or more business customers, where Customer Success has become a bottleneck but the business is not ready to build a large internal CS department. Common signs are founder led customer relationships, an overloaded CS team, inconsistent onboarding and no formal customer health model. What services are included? Four services: CS Foundation (a fixed scope build of your CS framework), Managed Customer Success (Booked runs Customer Success for your accounts), CS Team Extension (extra CSM capacity beside your team) and Customer Success Operations (CRM, health scoring, dashboards, automation and renewal workflows). How is it priced? Usually a one time setup fee plus a monthly retainer. The retainer is scoped by the number of managed accounts, their touch level, meeting cadence and reporting needs. CS Foundation and CS Operations projects are fixed scope. We do not bill by the hour except for tightly scoped projects. Do you guarantee retention or renewal rates? No. Retention and growth are outcomes the service is built to support, but product quality, pricing, customer budgets and market conditions also influence them. We agree two or three measurable success criteria at kickoff, such as onboarding completion, time to first value and at risk accounts actioned, and report against them every month. Which markets and time zones do you cover? We work with B2B SaaS companies globally and covers every time zone. Service hours, response times and the time zone they apply in are agreed up front and written into every contract, so your customers are looked after during their own working day, wherever they are. Is this the same team as your outsourced SDR service? No. Customer Success as a Service is run by a separate Booked division with its own team and methodology, and you can buy it on its own. Article Refining the backlog and the Definition of Ready In Scrum, everything revolves around the sprint, a clearly-defined, intensely productive period of time in which the team tackles priorities from the product backlog. But how does the Scrum team (including the product owner) know when those priorities are ready to be addressed? How do you know when it’s time to sprint? This is where the process of backlog refinement, filtered through what’s known as the Definition of Ready (DoR), plays an essential role. Clearly, the Definition of Ready and the refinement process are interdependent. Refinement results in product backlog items that are ready for development, and the Definition of Ready is the criteria by which we can say that refinement has been successful – if a Definition of Ready is at all unclear, you need to revisit the refinement process! Fractional Product Executive for B2B SaaS and AI Transformation | Erica Jenkins Skip to content How we help Sound familiar? Insights Resources About Start a conversation Scaling B2B SaaS is a marathon. Doing it while going AI-first is a gauntlet. I’m a fractional product executive for martech and big data SaaS, with 30,000+ hours, $500M+ in revenue, two acquisitions and an IPO behind me. With my bench of seasoned operators, we don’t just suggest change. We execute it, closing the gap between your vision and the tactical reality. Start a conversation See how we help Erica Jenkins, founder of Erica Jenkins Consulting The four root causes of stagnation Scaling from $10M to $30M ARR is hard enough. Trying to 5X that growth while moving to an AI-first architecture is harder, and “AI transformation” on its own won’t get you there. When growth stalls, it’s almost always one of these four. We fix them with your team, not around them. Innovation and tech debt AI isn’t a plug-in. It’s a foundational shift. We prioritize refactoring legacy infrastructure so tech debt doesn’t become AI bankruptcy, and modernize your stack so AI strengthens your product instead of bloating it. Leadership evolution The hands-on founder model breaks around $10M ARR. We help founders move from doer to architect, with fractional leaders running product, engineering and go-to-market while your internal team levels up. Operational communication Silos and egos block growth. We get product, sales and engineering working together on AI implementation, so internal automation turns into customer value instead of internal friction. Hardened processes We define and document the machine behind your SaaS, from AI-augmented customer onboarding to automated licensing, and build the repeatable playbooks that make you an attractive acquisition target. Three ways to work together We can work in your business, on your business or about your business. Each puts us at a different distance from your day-to-day, so choose the one that fits what you need now. Many clients move between them over time. Three rings around your team: In the business is closest, On the business is in the middle, About the business is outermost About On In Your team The closer the ring, the closer we work to your day-to-day. In the business Fractional Product Leader Two days a week, embedded with your team We lead product execution or a platform migration, set priorities, and build the habits that keep your company customer-centric and churn low. AI gets built into how your product team researches, plans and ships. On the business Product Optimization One day a week, across teams We assess how you build, launch and support your product, then put the roadmap process and playbooks in place so your teams work from the same plan, with AI and automation taking out manual work wherever it pays off. About the business Advisement Retainer Ten hours a month, cancel anytime Working sessions with your executives to unblock product, pricing and operating decisions, including where AI belongs in your strategy and where it doesn’t, with clear recommendations you can act on. Compare the engagements “ Fractional in title, full time on impact. Michelle A CEO & Founder What changes when we’re in the room Two recent engagements. Clients stay with us for two and a half years on average, so the work goes past recommendations into results. Media monitoring SaaS, $20M+ ARR From closed deal to customer login, automatically Before Every step from a signed deal to a working account was manual: someone had to set up the account, configure the package and send the welcome. Deal signed → Manual setup → Manual config → Manual welcome What we did With me as fractional head of product, we built a deal-to-provision flow that sets up each account automatically based on the package sold. Result Revenue leakage was eliminated due to automated provisioning, renewal and removing sales rep “giveaway” behaviors. We unlocked aggregated reporting of accounts. Deal signed → Automatic provisioning → Instant invite B2B SaaS company From feature factory to a story customers care about Before The roadmap was a feature factory, and every message explained how features worked, click by click. The company had also gone so far into product-led growth, down to buying on the website, that customers who needed help had no one to call. What we did We spent a quarter measuring the value customers actually got, then rebuilt the story around the problems the product solves. That reshaped the website and go-to-market, launched a customer newsletter and webinar series, and found a middle ground between self-serve and human help. Result −7% Churn dropped by 7%. With over 31.7 million active social media users in early 2025, representing approximately 79.4% of the population, Canada offers a robust market for social commerce initiatives. In 2024, the Canadian social commerce market was valued at USD $6.47 billion, and it is projected to reach USD $10.99 billion by 2029, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.2%. Key Trends and Strategic Insights 1. Platform Integration Retailers can establish virtual storefronts on platforms like Instagram Shops and TikTok Shop, enabling seamless in-app purchases. Product tagging in posts and videos allows for instant purchases, shortening the sales funnel. 2. Influencer Collaborations Partnering with Canadian influencers enhances product visibility and builds consumer trust. Influencer marketing is a powerful tool in driving engagement and conversions. 3. Logistics and Fulfillment Efficient cross-border shipping and reliable fulfillment partners are crucial for timely delivery and customer satisfaction. American companies should establish partnerships with logistics providers experienced in cross-border e-commerce. 4. Mobile Optimization Given the high percentage of mobile internet usage, ensuring mobile-friendly shopping experiences is essential. Most social commerce activity occurs on smartphones, making mobile optimization a priority. For U.S. companies aiming to expand into Canada, incorporating social commerce into their market strategies provides a powerful opportunity to engage a digitally savvy audience and grow sales with lower upfront costs. USA.gov | FOIA | Privacy Program | Disclaimer | Information Quality Guidelines | Accessibility × Global Business Navigator Chatbot Beta Welcome to the Global Business Navigator, an artificial intelligence (AI) Chatbot from the International Trade Administration (ITA). This tool, currently in beta version testing, is designed to provide general information on the exporting process and the resources available to assist new and experienced U.S. exporters. The Chatbot, developed using Microsoft’s Azure AI services, is trained on ITA’s export-related content and aims to quickly get users the information they need. The Chatbot is intended to make the benefits of exporting more accessible by understanding non-expert language, idiomatic expressions, and foreign languages. Limitations As a beta product, the Chatbot is currently being tested and its responses may occasionally produce inaccurate or incomplete information. The Chatbot is trained to decline out of scope or inappropriate requests. The Chatbot’s knowledge is limited to the public information on the Export Solutions web pages of Trade.gov, which covers a wide range of topics on exporting. While it cannot provide responses specific to a company’s product or a specific foreign market, its reference pages will guide you to other relevant government resources and market research. Always double-check the Chatbot’s responses using the provided references or by visiting the Export Solutions web pages on Trade.gov. Do not use its responses as legal or professional advice. Inaccurate advice from the Chatbot would not be a defense to violating any export rules or regulations. Privacy The Chatbot does not collect information about users and does not use the contents of users’ chat history to learn new information. All feedback is anonymous. Please do not enter personally identifiable information (PII), sensitive, or proprietary information into the Chatbot. Your conversations will not be connected to other interactions or accounts with ITA. Conversations with the Chatbot may be reviewed to help ITA improve the tool and address harmful, illegal, or otherwise inappropriate questions. Translation The Chatbot supports a wide range of languages. Because the Chatbot is trained in English and responses are translated, you should verify the translation. For example, the Chatbot may have difficulty with acronyms, abbreviations, and nuances in a language other than English. Privacy Program | Information Quality Guidelines | Accessibility
